lines.text: # Local patches to vendored code

Every place where `vendor/` differs from its upstream. Keep this list complete: add an entry with the patch, and remove it when the patch goes. Patches inside single headers are marked with a `VitaDeck:` comment where the diff allows one.

Unpatched, byte for byte upstream: `arena.h` ([tsoding/arena](https://github.com/tsoding/arena) `ab625dd`), `raylib.h` ([raysan5/raylib](https://github.com/raysan5/raylib) tag `5.5`), `stb_truetype.h` ([nothings/stb](https://github.com/nothings/stb) v1.26, `6e9f34d`).
## stb_ds.h: hash maps stop advancing the global seed
- Upstream: [nothings/stb](https://github.com/nothings/stb) `stb_ds.h` v0.67, last changed in `40adb995abeea13612ad73bda031c90e3c0cf821`.
- File: `vendor/stb_ds.h`, `stbds_make_hash_index`.

Upstream reads `stbds_hash_seed` for each new table and then advances it with an LCG, an unsynchronized write to a global from whichever thread creates the table. VitaDeck creates hash maps on both the JS thread (a fresh instance registry on every snapshot swap, timers) and the main thread (scroll offsets, glyph cache), so this is a data race (#78, fixed in #81). The patch drops the LCG and its locals and keeps the read; every table still stores its own seed, so they now all share the startup seed, which only matters for hash-flooding resistance VitaDeck does not need.

Why it cannot live in `src/`: no `STBDS_*` option disables the advance, and calling `stbds_rand_seed` once at startup does not help because every later table creation writes the seed again. Avoiding it from `src/` would mean confining every hash map creation to one thread, which the per-swap registry on the JS thread and the lazily created main-thread maps rule out. Checked under TSan with `snapshot_swap_harness` (Linux smoke image, `-DVITADECK_SANITIZE=thread`): upstream reports the race in `stbds_make_hash_index` between `deep_copy_instance` and `scroll.c`'s `ensure_map`, the patched header runs clean.

Replay: in `stbds_make_hash_index`, delete the `size_t a,b,temp;` declaration and the four `// LCG` lines that update `stbds_hash_seed` in the `else` branch, leaving `t->seed = stbds_hash_seed;` with the `VitaDeck:` comment. Drop the patch if upstream makes the seed thread-safe.
## jimp/jimp.h: Vita GCC warning fixes
- Upstream: [tsoding/jim](https://github.com/tsoding/jim) `jimp.h` at `2890b452593c4a108d209db16d5a19c6ce5f9982` (see `jimp/README.md`, ADR 0003).
- File: `vendor/jimp/jimp.h`, `jimp__skip_whitespaces` and `jimp_diagf`.

Two one-token changes so the Vita build is warning-free: the `isspace` argument is cast to `unsigned char` (char subscript warning, and UB for negative chars), and the column in the diagnostic `fprintf` uses `%td` for a pointer difference instead of `%ld`. No behaviour change on the host.
Replay: re-apply both edits after copying a new `jimp.h`; `diff` against upstream should show exactly these two lines.
## quickjs: Vita platform guards (submodule fork)
- Upstream: [bellard/quickjs](https://github.com/bellard/quickjs) `e5fd3918c1c4a2ee39016e71b66a9eeda85ce716` (`VERSION` 2025-09-13).
- Fork: the submodule points at [matemolnar8/quickjs](https://github.com/matemolnar8/quickjs) `e8951c960cd2ac451f7a1500dee465aeaa1b8f33`, one commit ("Vita") on top of that upstream commit.
- File: `quickjs.c`.

Adds `__vita__` to four platform checks in `quickjs.c` so it builds and links against the Vita newlib: `CONFIG_ATOMICS` and `CONFIG_STACK_CHECK` stay undefined, `js_def_malloc_usable_size` returns 0 like Emscripten, and `getTimezoneOffset` takes the `_WIN32` path that derives the offset from `gmtime`/`localtime` instead of `tm_gmtoff`. The fork commit has no message beyond "Vita"; the reasons are the platform gaps the guards route around.

Replay: in the fork, rebase the "Vita" commit onto the new upstream commit (`git fetch https://github.com/bellard/quickjs master && git rebase FETCH_HEAD`), push the fork, then bump the submodule here and run the Vita Docker build.
- License: MIT, copied in `LICENSE`
Local patches:
- Cast the `isspace` argument to `unsigned char` so Vita GCC does not warn about
char subscripts.
- Print pointer differences with `%td` so Vita GCC does not warn about the
diagnostic column format.
Local patches: two Vita GCC warning fixes, recorded in `../PATCHES.md`.
VitaDeck uses this header only behind the native `package_manifest` module.
Do not expose `jimp` types through VitaDeck interfaces.

lines.text: **Considered options:** use one cross-language package-format source of truth now (rejected as too much tooling for the current need); preserve the hand-written JSON scanners (rejected because it keeps low locality); use `jsmn` (rejected because token walking is less readable for this module); use `sheredom/json.h` first (kept as backup because it compiled cleanly on Vita but is less aligned with the desired immediate-mode reader).

**Consequences:** vendor `jimp.h` under a subdirectory with provenance notes and the Vita warning fixes. Add a focused `package_manifest` CTest harness for manifest acceptance and rejection cases. Keep TypeScript SDK package-format cleanup as an explicit follow-up rather than mixing it into this native refactor.

**Consequences:** vendor `jimp.h` under a subdirectory with provenance notes and the Vita warning fixes, recorded in `vendor/PATCHES.md` with every other local vendor patch. Add a focused `package_manifest` CTest harness for manifest acceptance and rejection cases. Keep TypeScript SDK package-format cleanup as an explicit follow-up rather than mixing it into this native refactor.
